items.title: Norman Brownlee Interview, 1961-05-05
items.q: They had my band, and I had a, I had a very good aggregation there that night from the sense of musicians. I mean, it was like, like Pinky Vedakovich on sax and Jordy on sax. And, uh, uh, Baduk on drums, Billy Braun on mellophone, uh, Joe Lorcanna trombone.

ctx.x: Oh, that's who I was trying to think.

Billy Braun, he played piano. And, uh, many times, rehearse the band with, uh, numbers. A new number come out, Billy would play it, see? And we might say, play it again. And he'd play it again, and, uh, then, uh, then we'd take it. He'd switch over. But, uh, we were playing, uh, we were playing the, uh, the Spinsters Ball in, uh, Biloxi, Mississippi. A carnival ball. And they had two bands. They had my band, and I had a, I had a very good aggregation there that night from the sense of musicians. I mean, it was…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: And then later on, I played a couple of jobs with the band, see. And he had Brownlee playing piano

ctx.x: Well, on our intermission, at least around noon, we'd go get our lunch and we'd go out to the street. He'd bring his corner out there and take a pair of sticks and cymbals and so forth. And Eastwood would take his banjo and we'd have a jam session. Mm-hmm. And we had a wonderful time together on our intermission on 12 o'clock lunch. And then later on, I played a couple of jobs with the band, see. And he had Brownlee playing piano and Emmett Hardy playing cornet and so forth. And then later on, later on I played…
Yeah, it's still there. It's exterminated.
